A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RealRAG. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the added Appendix C in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and classification results, retrieval ablations, and a 26-participant human evaluation, including results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, and human-evaluation outcomes in the main text and appendices. These retained results qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The specified training objective changes locally: Eq. 7 exponentiates the in-batch similarities, and Eq. 8 moves temperature scaling inside the numerator's exponential. The reflective-negative selection and retrieval-conditioned generation pipeline remain intact; these formula corrections do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet and the Cars, Dogs, and Flowers datasets for database construction, the same three fine-grained evaluation benchmarks, and the same novel-object cases. Appendix C discusses multimodal, 3D, and video applications without evaluating them.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain OmniGen, Emu, SD V2.1, SD XL, SD V3, and Flux. Tables 3 and 5 retain Zero-RAG and Normal-RAG comparisons using Emu, SD V2.1, and Flux. Newly cited retrieval-augmented diffusion methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The training/test split usage, ten generated images per class, FID/CLIP metrics, OpenCLIP classification evaluation, and human-study procedures remain unchanged. The added conditioning and Google Images descriptions disclose details of existing experiments without establishing revised protocols.

E4.justification: The retrieval ablations in Tables 3 and 5, checkpoint comparisons in Figure 7, t-SNE analyses in Figures 8 and 12, and qualitative cases are retained. The new discussion and application appendix introduce no additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the same human-rating error bars and accompanying mean/variance discussion. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the empirical plots retain their results; for example, Emu's Stanford Cars FID remains 86.73 without RealRAG and 70.55 with it. Generated examples and t-SNE point data are unchanged. The corrected Audi name in the prose matches the already-present Figure 4 panel.

T1.justification: Eq. 7 replaces a sum of temperature-scaled similarities with a sum of their exponentials, while Eq. 8 replaces exp(s)/tau with exp(s/tau) in the numerator. These are non-equivalent corrections to the mathematical loss definition. No new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of a real-object-based RAG framework, self-reflective retrieval of missing knowledge, compatibility across generator families, and improved fine-grained and novel-object realism. Removing the introductory human-evaluation summary does not remove that claim from the paper.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly defines novel objects relative to generator and retriever training times. Appendix C adds training-cost motivation and application discussion. However, Section 6 describes RealRAG as training or fine-tuning diffusion models, conflicting with the frozen generator in Section 3.2 and the no-retraining rationale in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies native image conditioning for autoregressive models and ControlNet conditioning for diffusion models. Section 4.3 identifies Google Images as the novel-object reference source. The introduction replaces the future code-release promise with a project-page link, without establishing code availability within the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and brief positioning around artistic retrieval-augmented diffusion, kNN-Diffusion, ReImagen, vision RAG, and downstream multimodal/3D/video applications. Most existing related-work exposition remains intact. The new RDM comparison is unclear because it assigns identical purposes to prior methods and RealRAG.

P1.justification: v2 adds short Discussion and Application Value sections, implementation explanations, and acknowledgments. It corrects LIANG to LAION and the AR example from Audi 100 Wagon 1994 to Audi TT Hatchback 2011, alongside author/correspondence edits. Most existing prose and organization are retained.

P2.justification: All thirteen figures and five tables remain. v2 changes Figure 1's illustrative similarity bars, removes numerical axis markings from the t-SNE displays, relocates Figure 8, enlarges and relocates Table 3, and adjusts headers and spacing. These are limited presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The corrected loss equations and newly documented conditioning mechanism resolve concrete technical ambiguities in v1, providing a limited improvement in clarity and reproducibility. The empirical evidence is unchanged. This gain is tempered by Section 6's duplicated RDM comparison and its fine-tuning description, which conflicts with the frozen-generator account elsewhere in v2.
